0.advice_hint: Prune affected leaves and fallen debris to reduce fungal spores. Apply preventative copper or sulfur fungicides before rainy periods.

1.advice_hint: Prune out dead wood, mummified fruits, and cankers. Spray with appropriate fungicide from petal fall through harvest.

2.advice_hint: Remove nearby cedar or juniper galls if feasible. Treat with myclobutanil or sulfur fungicide at bud break.

3.advice_hint: Plant appears healthy. Continue balanced watering, mulching, and routine nutrient management.

4.advice_hint: Bush is healthy. Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5–5.5) and keep soil consistently moist with organic mulch.

5.advice_hint: Ensure adequate sunlight and air circulation through pruning. Apply potassium bicarbonate or sulfur sprays upon first sign.

6.advice_hint: Cherry foliage is healthy. Maintain regular pruning and avoid moisture buildup around root collars.

7.advice_hint: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops and bury crop residue. Apply foliar fungicide if lesions appear before tasseling.

8.advice_hint: Plant resistant hybrid varieties. Fungicides are generally only needed if pustules spread heavily before silking.

9.advice_hint: Rotate crops and manage debris to break disease cycle. Apply recommended fungicides if lesions develop early in upper canopy.

10.advice_hint: Crop is healthy and vigorous. Maintain nitrogen scheduling and monitor soil moisture during flowering.

11.advice_hint: Remove mummified berries from vines and ground. Spray mancozeb or captan from bud break until veraison.

12.advice_hint: Prune infected vines during dry periods and protect pruning wounds. Remove heavily symptomatic wood to prolong vine life.

13.advice_hint: Prune canopy to promote air movement and sunlight penetration. Apply copper oxychloride or protectant fungicide sprays.

14.advice_hint: Vine foliage is healthy. Keep canopy well-trained on trellises and avoid water stress during berry formation.

15.advice_hint: Control Asian citrus psyllid vectors immediately with horticultural oils or insecticides. Remove severely infected trees to protect surrounding orchards.

16.advice_hint: Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers which stimulate succulent growth. Apply copper bactericides during dormancy and oxytetracycline during the season.

17.advice_hint: Foliage is healthy. Maintain routine orchard sanitation and thin fruit for optimal canopy airflow.

18.advice_hint: Use certified disease-free seeds and avoid overhead irrigation. Apply copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb to slow spread.

19.advice_hint: Pepper plant is healthy. Support with stakes and maintain consistent soil moisture to prevent blossom end rot.

20.advice_hint: Remove infected lower foliage and avoid overhead sprinkling. Spray chlorothalonil or copper fungicides at initial symptom onset.

21.advice_hint: Urgent: destroy infected vines immediately to prevent tuber rot. Spray systemic fungicides such as metalaxyl or dimethomorph promptly.

22.advice_hint: Plant appears vigorous and healthy. Hill soil around stems and monitor regularly during cool, humid weather.

23.advice_hint: Canes are healthy. Prune out floricanes post-harvest and ensure well-draining organic soil.

24.advice_hint: Foliage is healthy. Ensure adequate potassium levels and scout weekly for defoliating pests.

25.advice_hint: Space vines to improve airflow and water at soil base. Apply neem oil, potassium bicarbonate, or sulfur fungicide at first spots.

26.advice_hint: Remove infected old leaves after harvest and plant resistant cultivars. Apply protective copper sprays in spring.

27.advice_hint: Plants are healthy. Keep straw mulch beneath fruit and water with drip lines to keep crowns dry.

28.advice_hint: Avoid overhead watering and working in wet foliage. Treat with copper-based sprays combined with mancozeb.

29.advice_hint: Prune lower leaves touching soil and apply thick organic mulch. Spray copper fungicide or chlorothalonil every 7-10 days in wet conditions.

30.advice_hint: Highly destructive fungal pathogen: isolate and dispose of affected plant parts immediately. Apply preventative copper or mancozeb.

31.advice_hint: Lower humidity in greenhouses and maximize ventilation. Spray copper fungicides upon detecting olive-green mold underneath leaves.

32.advice_hint: Strip bottom infected leaves immediately to stop upward progression. Apply fungicidal spray and practice 3-year crop rotation.

33.advice_hint: Wash undersides of leaves with strong water spray or apply insecticidal soap/neem oil. Release predatory mites in greenhouse settings.

34.advice_hint: Improve row spacing and prune inner suckers for airflow. Apply azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil fungicides as directed.

35.display_name: Tomato - Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
35.advice_hint: Virus transmitted by whiteflies: install yellow sticky traps and apply insecticidal soap. Rogue out infected plants to protect healthy ones.

36.advice_hint: No chemical cure: sanitize hands and pruning shears thoroughly; avoid tobacco contact. Remove and burn heavily infected plants.

37.advice_hint: Plant is vibrant and healthy. Maintain consistent drip irrigation, cage/stake support, and balanced fertilization.
